children: Abraxas Capital Management withdrew a total of 17,597 BTC, worth about $1.04 billion, from centralized exchanges while Bitcoin traded below $60,000, at an average price of about $59,206, according to on-chain tracker Lookonchain. On-chain analyst EmberCN said 11,241 BTC (about $670 million) of that total was withdrawn as BTC rebounded above $60,000, and suggested the buying was likely what drove the rebound.Garrett Jin deposited a cumulative $65 million in stablecoins to centralized exchanges on November 21 and posted "time to bid," BlockBeats reported. Lookonchain also flagged a wallet suspected to belong to Jin that deposited $270 million in stablecoins that day, though Odaily noted there is no evidence confirming the wallet's ownership or the purpose of the funds.BTC fell to about $55,632 around 14:15 UTC+8 on November 21, returned above $60,000 around 21:40 UTC+8 that evening, and traded around the $60,000 mark through the morning of November 22, peaking at about $60,362, CoinMarketCap data showed. As of 12:17 UTC+8, BTC was at $59,330, up 6.22% over 24 hours and down 8.48% over seven days.

title: Abraxas Capital, Other Whales Buy the BTC Dip as Bitcoin Briefly Reclaims $60,000
